tldr this in 5 bullets:

The city council voted on Tuesday to approve a revised transit plan that extends the light rail line by eleven kilometres and adds four stations in the eastern districts. (Section 1.1) 

Supporters argued that the extension would cut commute times for roughly forty thousand residents, while opponents raised concerns about construction noise and the cost, which has risen by nearly a fifth since the first estimate. (Section 1.2) 

A spokesperson for the transit authority said the project is on schedule, although a shortage of tunnelling crews could push the opening date into the following year. (Section 1.3) 

Local businesses along the planned route are divided; some expect more foot traffic, others fear that years of roadworks will drive customers away. (Section 1.4) 

Environmental groups welcomed the plan but asked for stricter limits on dust and vibration during excavation, and for guaranteed funding for replacement trees. (Section 1.5) 

The mayor described the vote as a turning point and promised quarterly public updates, adding that a citizens panel would review every major contract. (Section 1.6) 

Economists consulted by the paper estimated the line could add several percentage points to property values near new stations within a decade. (Section 1.7)
